articles.title: Borderlands 4 Is Cheaper Than Ever Before for Black Friday
articles.summary: Borderlands 4 is seeing a huge discount, marked down a massive 79%, which brings its price to just $15. This deal comes in time for Black Friday and makes it one of the best opportunities to jump into the series' latest entry. With how expensive AAA gaming has become, sales like these can save players' […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Borderlands 4 is seeing a huge discount, marked down a massive 79%, which brings its price to just $15. This deal comes in time for Black Friday and makes it one of the best opportunities to jump into the series' latest entry. With how expensive AAA gaming has become, sales like these can save players' wallets. The industry often sees many of the most popular games go on sale for Black Friday and the holidays, but discounts of this magnitude are not generally seen. There is no telling how long Borderlands 4's sale will go on or if it will sell out, so fans should act quickly.

The deal can be found on Amazon and other retailers, where the physical version of Borderlands 4 on PlayStation 5 is marked down to $15.00 , making it the lowest price the game has seen since its release in 2025 . There may never be another sale this low. The latest entry in the popular looter shooter series offers another opportunity to hunt down legendary weapons, experiment with character builds, and cause chaos alongside friends. It is worth it at full price, but this sale makes purchasing it a no-brainer for anyone on the fence.

Discounts vary depending on your platform and whether you prefer physical or digital games, with PS5 offering the best deal at $15.00. That said, Xbox Series X players can get their hands on a physical copy between $15.00 and $19.99. Sadly, PC players are not as lucky as a code for Borderlands 4 still runs $49.99. Sadly, there is no option for Nintendo Switch players . These deals are available on Amazon , Best Buy , Target , and GameStop .

There is no stated period for the sale, so it could very well end after Black Friday. Physical editions could also see limited stock and may sell out before you can purchase a copy. Digital versions do not have this worry, but the physical versions offer the best sale currently.

For those unfamiliar with Borderlands 4 , Gearbox takes players away from Pandora and introduces them to Kairos, a planet ruled by the Timekeeper. Players can choose from four new Vault Hunters, each featuring distinct abilities and skill trees. It has enhanced the exploration aspect with new abilities and mechanics, making traversal and combat more dynamic.

One of the biggest draws of the Borderlands series has always been its cooperative multiplayer, and that is true here. Borderlands 4 supports up to four players in online co-op, with individual difficulty settings and level scaling to accommodate different skill levels. That said, it can also be enjoyed solo, even if multiplayer is a more full experience. Players can expect between 30 and 100 hours of chaotic shooting fun in Borderlands 4 , and now for the low price of $15.

articles.title: How 'The Lowdown' Season 2 Finale Sets Up a (Hoped for) Third Season
articles.summary: Creator Sterlin Harjo and Ethan Hawke break down Lee's growth as a person and the loose threads still left to explore.
articles.content:
[This story contains spoilers for season two of The Lowdown and "The Tower," the Nov. 25 season finale.]

The first season of The Lowdown had a pretty clear resolution : The story that "truthstorian" Lee Raybon ( Ethan Hawke ) had been chasing throughout the season — about the death of the brother (Tim Blake Nelson) of Oklahoma's likely next governor (Kyle Maclachlan) and their family's corrupt history — was printed (if not in the form he initially thought) and seemingly put to rest.

Season two, however, concludes with multiple threads still untied — and some even circling back to season one. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV 'American Horror Story' Finale: Paul Anthony Kelly on the Season 13 Ending: "I Was Flabbergasted" TV 'Snowfall' Spinoff Boss Malcolm Spellman Lays Out Multi-Season Plan for 'The Drop,' Why Season One Was Just a "Dash of What's Coming"

Lee, with help from some of the journalists he disparaged at the beginning of the season, gets an exposé on conditions at Judge Sallsman's (John Hawkes) Fresh Start meatpacking operations published, but he's frustrated that he can't tie the judge himself to the story. As he continues chasing leads — including getting Martha Plimpton's Sheriff Thorne to go on record about the judge — Marty (Keith David) saves Lee from walking into a confrontation with some of the people behind last season's One Well conspiracy. They realize that Lee's story about Fresh Start, the One Well people and Marty's investigation of the illicit sale of indigenous artifacts are all part of a bigger picture. Ginger (Betty Gilpin), meanwhile, leaves Tulsa after realizing that, for several reasons, she can't continue her life there.

In other words, there is a lot left to explore in a potential third season — which FX hasn't decided on yet.

"I'm trying to twist their arm," The Lowdown creator and showrunner Sterlin Harjo told The Hollywood Reporter about the very open-ended finale. "We left it open and pushed forward to a season three because I like three-season shows. I don't know if we're going to be doing it, but I hope that we are." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The finale, titled "The Tower," did offer closure on one front: Lee, his daughter Francis (Ryan Kiera Armstrong) and their family and friends lay Tommy Lee Jones' Lee Sr., aka Frog, to rest at a somewhat chaotic funeral, which features the return of Peter Dinklage as Lee's friend Wendell, who eulogizes Frog with a reading of Dylan Thomas' "Do Not Go Gentle Into That Good Night." That's followed by a more relaxed, and touching, gathering at Sweet Emily's afterward, where Francis reads a journal entry of Frog's detailing the apprehension he felt about being a father when Lee was a baby.

"He's going through the stages of grief. How he understands and reinterprets he and his father's relationship now that his father's gone, it's going to be an ever-changing thing," Hawke tells THR . Unfortunately, it does not add back any of the removed features , nor is it particularly substantial. Many were expecting and hoping for a significant first update, as is often customary with games, at least when the first update takes a little bit of time. This is not the case, though. This first Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake doesn't do much.

The new Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake update is specifically the 1.1.2 update. And while it doesn't do much, Nintendo has provided the patch notes for it, which consist of two lines. One of these notes the new Zelda update fixes "several issues" that will provide a smother smoother gameplay experience. How many fixed issues are contained within this, we don't know. Could be a few, dozens, or even hundreds. Unfortunately, Nintendo patch notes aren't the most transparent, and these are no exception.

There is one fix it felt the need to highlight, though, which is the other line of the patch notes. This line reveals Nintendo has fixed the event where "Malon's Event" could not be progressed. This being highlighted suggests every other fix lumped together in the other line is less significant than this one; otherwise, it would be highlighted as well. This doesn't narrow the field much, though, because this is a pretty substantial fix.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is available via the Nintendo Switch 2, and the Nintendo Switch 2 only.

articles.title: Happy Thanksgiving, Netflix Just Canceled Two Shows With Major Stars
articles.summary: The streaming service is at it again.
articles.content:
Thanksgiving is officially upon us, and many TV and movie fans are going to be re-watching their favorite festive programming. Whether its Friends ' Thanksgiving episodes or a trip to Star's Hallow from Gilmore Girls , there's plenty to chose from. Unfortunately we got some bad news for TV addicts, specifically those with a Netflix subscription . Namely that the streaming platform has cancelled two more shows after just one season , and they both star big celebrities.

Then there's Amsterdam Empire , which had arguably less hype around it than Ferrell's comedy series. Starring Famke Janssen ( Goldeneye , The X-Men movies ), the show followed her character Betty Jonkers, a former pop star whose coffee-mogul husband is hiding some shady dealings. The show was shot entirely in Dutch, which is the accomplished actress' first language. Unfortunately the show is now over after just one season, which ended on an exciting cliffhanger. This comes after Janssen was noticeably left out of Avengers: Doomsday , despite so many of her X-Men co-stars reprising their roles in the upcoming Marvel movie .

These two titles join the ranks of many shows that Netflix has dropped way too early, to dismay of fans. Some other titles to have suffered this fate include The OA , which was cancelled after two wild seasons and a huge cliffhanger. Then there was Sense8 , which got cancelled but eventually got a movie finale after fans made their voices known. Fans have also been hoping to see more of David Fincher's Mindhunter since the last episode aired back in 2019.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google As families gather around the dinner table for the winter holidays, there's one feeling that invades their bodies more than upset stomachs from undercooked turkey. It's the dread and anxiety that come with being forced around family members who you would otherwise never volunteer to see, let alone joining them to eat a meal. Most Thanksgiving TV specials focus on gratitude and finding a middle ground to get along with relatives, but there is a reason those shows are fiction and not real-life. There's one episode of a classic sci-fi show that happens to take place on Thanksgiving, and its table-side etiquette will remind you that things could always be worse, especially if your guest has unlimited cosmic powers at their beckon.

"Charlie X" from Star Trek's debut season is a great example of a sci-fi trope that continues to be played out in the genre to this very day. It centers on an overpowered being with little grasp on humanity and how to be responsible with their abilities, resulting in some very uncomfortable situations for Captain Kirk's crew. The storyline is only a Thanksgiving episode due to its apparent stardate and a handful of throwaway lines of dialogue, but it actually has a hidden holiday message that you might want to take to the heart to your next family gathering. Or, you can learn a piece of obscure Star Trek trivia that very few people are aware of and use that to escape a conversation with your very politically-charged aunt or uncle . The choice is yours, which is more than we can say for poor Charlie.

"Charlie X" was part of the first draft proposal Roddenberry used to shop the series around in 1964. Under the working title of "The Day Charlie Became God," its synopsis read as "the accidental occurrence of infinite power to do all things, in the hands of a very finite man." No mention was made of how old this mortal being was, but making them into a moody teenager was a genius play that was a perfect fit for this script. When the finalized version aired on Sep. 15, 1966, the series had only just started and NBC viewers were still getting used to the idea of creator Gene Roddenberry's vision for " Wagon Train to the stars." What they weren't prepared for was intergalactic teenage melodrama along with their sci-fi that made for an hour of unexpectedly good television.

Strange things start happening on board the USS Enterprise after picking up Charlie Evans, a socially awkward teen who spent nearly all of his life alone on an uninhabited planet. Not only are they weird in the sense of odd coincidences happening whenever Charlie is around such as playing cards changing face or Thanksgiving meals appearing out of thin air (more on that later), but dangerous such as starships exploding to smithereens or crew members mysteriously disappearing when he is angered. It doesn't take long for Kirk, Spock and McCoy to suss out what is happening, and deduce that their adolescent passenger may be a Thasian, a race of extremely powerful beings in the same vein as Trelane or a member of the Q Continuum . However, those aliens are non-corporeal, and Dr. McCoy's scans prove Charlie is a human. The problem then becomes how do you discipline a spiteful teen boy with raging hormones who can snap his finger and make everyone disappear?

After Charlie's secret is exposed, he stops trying to hide his desires and commandeers the starship with his powers to fast travel to Colony Alpha V, the last known home of any of his relatives. His list of victims rapidly grows, as he turns one girl he liked into an iguana while another female crew member has her face completely removed. Kirk knows Charlie can destroy their entire vessel whenever he feels like it, so he and his advisors work quietly to find a way to stop him. As their plan takes shape and begins to work, an unexpected non-corporeal visitor arrives — a representative from Thasius who explains who Charlie is and how he was gifted his powers. Just as easily as Charlie was given his powers, so too can they take them, and the green entity beams a screaming Charlie away to be taught a lesson in respect and possibly worse.

This offbeat episode holds one unique distinction in Star Trek history as being the only episode of the series that Roddenberry performed in. While Roddenberry was credited as Producer and writer (even though D.C. Fontana developed the story and wrote the teleplay), he was also an actor in "Charlie X." His role as the galley chef seen towards the end of the first act is partially obscured by set decoration and hidden by him turning his back to the camera, leaving this Easter Egg as a special one for those hardcore Trekkies in the know. Roddenberry's fleeting Trek cameo is also the moment where we learn the date of when these events unfold. "On Earth today it's Thanksgiving," Captain Kirk explains to the cook. "If the crew has to eat synthetic meatloaf, I want it to look like Turkey." His voice can be heard later in the episode after Charlie destroys the Antares, explaining that real turkeys suddenly appeared baking in the oven, a surprise to Kirk that starts him questioning who his new passenger truly is. Oh, and those turkeys for the ship's Thanksgiving dinner were probably burnt to a crisp during Charlie's tantrum turned takeover, so their meal for the evening was likely more of those pastel-colored cubes that never seemed very appetizing to begin with.

Star Trek has featured many great feasts over the years, including the awkward dinner between Kirk's crew and the Klingons in Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country , and "Forget Me Not" from Discovery's third season. There's even still time for a Thanksgiving Celebration while war rages on in Deep Space Nine , as there's a mention of Captain Sisko's impressive homemade turkey dinner with all the trimmings during "Blaze of Glory" from its fifth season. But as far as rough Thanksgiving celebrations go, none could be as brutal as Charlie X's visit to the Enterprise. Unseasoned mashed potatoes and cold turkey are nothing in comparison to having your eyes, mouth and nose wiped away from your face. So remember when you are eating your pecan pie while watching the clock tick down so you can make your getaway from your relatives to avoid another intense discussion about American politics and "the problem with today's generation," be grateful that none of them have godlike powers that could warp you to the Gamma Quadrant without an EV suit. Now, please pass the sweet potatoes — I've got some TOS to binge.

What did you think of "Charlie X" as an episode? Is it a must-watch or an easy pass? Join the conversation and let us know in the comments.

articles.title: One Thing Stephen Colbert Neglected While He Was On Late Night His Wife Wants Him To Get Into
articles.summary: I totally see how this happened.
articles.content:
It’s hard to believe The Late Show with Stephen Colbert has been off of the air for half a year now. It’s presence was so undeniable for so long, sometimes I still feel like it’s around even though it’s definitely cancelled . Stephen Colbert ’s kept busy, of course. He’s writing an LOTR movie (though we’ll have to see how it pans out after that merger )! Now that he does have more downtime he’s said there’s something his wife wants him to get into.

The man was taking a slew of questions from his fellow late night hosts in a profile with THR when he admitted to wanting to get fit, fit, fit. The only time I’ve ever seen Stephen Colbert really attempt anything related to fitness was like eight years ago when The Late Show did an interview with the late Ruth Bader Ginsberg that included mobility stretches and some minor lifting, oh and one shot of Stephen Colbert pulling up his shirt and exposing his all-time dad bod.

I can hardly blame the former late night host for not making the time for exercise. We learned a few months ago his writing team was working long hours and making monologue changes on the fly in order to stay ahead of social media during their later filming days. The thanks they got was getting fired and having just a few days to exit the studio . His stuff was shipped off to a museum. He went to his brother’s wedding, and then moved on. The one upside is now he has all the time in the world to get into shape.

So far, we haven’t seen Stephen Colbert become a fitness influencer in the days since The Late Show ended. However, there’s always time, and I will certainly be keeping my eyes peeled the next time the former late night host makes an appearance. Is that arm definition? Is there any hint of abs? Only time will tell.
